item.title: Headphone market sucks dick
item.description:
Did I fuck up buying these or is this a total audiochud victory?
I'm by no means an audiophile I don't even have an amp or dac. However the difference between some crap stereo speakers, "gayming" headphones, bluetooth earbuds and proper open-back studio headphones is night and fucking day.

I was looking up studio headphones around $200-$500 and I was really disappointed by the selection in this price range.
>Widespread chinkraisin lack of quality control (Hifiman mostly)
>Overpriced overrated 10-20 year old designs still going for MSRP or more (Sennheiser, Beyerdynamic)
>lack of features, comfort, aesthetics and utility (like who the fuck is going to buy a pair for $250-$300 that doesn't have detachable cables or doesn't fit well on every head shape?)
>ugly glossy plastic frames
I understand for the most part you get what you pay for, but in terms of headphones this simply isn't true. The quality in this price range is hit or miss.
Spending more doesn't really help either. I can't justify spending double my budget for some raisin that will be marginally better than something less than half the price.
A lot of the expensive pairs $800 to $$$$whatever are not for me, the average consumer, but there really isn't anything else with the same premium quality under that range.
I'm not going to buy some piece of fucking planned obsolescence CACA that is bound to break, which most budget models are.
But so many audiophile FAGGOTS are so content with settling for decade old slop brand headphones because some streamer uses them.
The entire "budget" headphone market is just one big capitulation on what you value more - bragging rights, comfort, specific features, or sound preference. A lot of the audiophiles are just consoimers seeking validation for their 10th luxury headphone and amp purchase which doesn't help the budget consumer in finding balanced reviews for raisin in their price range.

My first budget open-backs (Audio Technica ATH AD700x) have lasted me 6 years. They just died a couple days ago.
Compared to my old headphones which were logitech and stereo with a kill-myself tier memoryfoam headband, this was a huge upgrade for me.
I felt like the bass was a little quiet often times but other than that I loved them for general use.
From day 1 I had comfort problems due to the raisin Audio Technica patented wing design digging into my skull and not holding up which I was able to fix with a foam cushion.
Despite not really loving it, I didn't want to toss them in the trash.
They were already fully dead before I started trying to repair them so no risk and 100% reward if the repair worked.
The cable was broken inside the shell so it was a straight forward job, just cut the wire and resolder and reattach the internals.
Unfortunately I fucked up because the tiny 3.5cm wide circuit board made it impossible to get a good joint on and I ended up lifting a <5mm copper solderpad right off the board along with a trace.
On top of this, I was burning the edges of the plastic holding the board on and the external rubber lining (on the aux cord itself, not a result of this repair) was already really brittle and is going to break again.
So I was forced to buy a new pair.

All that mess aside, after a couple days of reading and watching reviews with captions on, I finally settled on a pair. pic rel
>ATH-R50x
>Detachable cables
>similar sound profile to my broken pair
>newer design from this year 2025
>Open-back
>universally comfortable (no wing-POS-design thank god)
>decent durability
>good repairability
>light
>not entirely plastic
>below my budget but apparently quite decent compared to models in the $500+ range
Listening to the reviews I think I struck gold in the budget market?
Since this is such a new model not very many headfi and reddit faggots have opinions on it and very few opinionated comparisons have been made to the usual cans (6xx, DT 990, etc).
Don't know how likely it is but I'm wondering if there is something better out there? I guess I'll give impressions on it if this thread is still up when it arrives.

item.title: Rambo Sucks
item.description:
I read First Blood by David Morrel a few years ago, and I thought it was decent.

I just watched Rambo 1 and 2 this week. I found them both boring.

Rambo 1 sort of glosses over things the book goes into better detail on. The way Rambo deals with the helicopter was much more interesting than in the movie, where he just tosses a rock at it.

Most of the movie after he escapes just feels like filler until the last scene where he's caught.

The performances by the actor playing Sam Trautman look like fucking AI raisin. It's really unnerving and disgusting, and fortunately he doesn't continue these fucking bizzare facial expressions in the sequel.

I kind of expected Rambo 2 to be like Predator but without the sci-fi element. It was dull. It looked and felt very cheap. The constant jumpcuts during the action made it feel like a hongkong martial arts movie, where they need to do 8 jumpcuts in a 3 second scene, to make you believe someone was able to jump really high.

I felt nothing when the Vietnamese love interest died. I'm sure MGS1 ripped off the torture scene, but they still did it better.

It doesn't really make sense that they don't have him cuffed when they put him on radio, and he had no way of knowing that the vietnamese woman was ready to help him, so it just feels like he escapes, because the movie needs him to escape at that moment, and not for any logical reason.

When Rambo explains he's expendable in the middle of the movie and at the end of the movie when he complains to Trautman about he wishes his country loved him as much as he loves it, it just feels like forced soapboxing.

I really felt like these sucked ass.

Do these movies have a lot of passionate defenders? Am I gonna find out I was stepping on people's toes, here?

I'm surprised how much I liked the Rambo movies despite not caring anything about sports.

item.title: The real meaning of The Shining
item.description:
I was listening to the Shining's opening theme last night and it occurred to me that it sounds like the soft feet of a ghost walking (the trumpets) as it passes by traumatizing memories (the various wailing and crying sounds).

I think this is a kind of emotional summary of what The Shining is about: evil, aka darkness.

Let me elaborate.

First off, I want to say that, if you're trying to find some cryptic message or hidden meaning in this film, you're going in the wrong direction. Like other famous horror films, it's just meant to scare you, but it exploits a deeper fear than the typical slasher film.

The fear that The Shining evokes is one that emerges from sadness, and everything about the movie is designed for this. The aforementioned soundtrack, the way it's shot, the setting, and the story.

Now there are two main parts that really drive The Shining's horror factor: the Overlook and Jack.

I'll start with the Overlook.

It's a place built on atrocities and tragedy from the very beginning, having its origins in the native American genocide. And beyond that it has a history of other tragedies and grim events. The Overlook is analogous to this black, demonic kind of darkness.

The other half of the puzzle is Jack. Have you ever been so angry or in any bad state of mind to the point that you truly felt like you could hurt innocent people? I'm sure many of you have. I have. Hell, that was part of King's inspiration for the book. And it's a scary experience seeing that side of you.

Well that's the core of Jack Torrance's character and that's what makes the story itself terrifying. Watching him fully embrace evil (more on that later) and cut through the thin veil of "happiness" his family had before they went to the Overlook.

item.description:
Hearing the difference now isn't the reason to encode to FLAC. FLAC uses lossless compression, while MP3 is 'lossy'. What this means is that for each year the MP3 sits on your hard drive, it will lose roughly 12kbps, assuming you have SATA - it's about 15kbps on IDE, but only 7kbps on SCSI, due to rotational velocidensity. You don't want to know how much worse it is on CD-ROM or other optical media.

I started collecting MP3s in about 2001, and if I try to play any of the tracks I downloaded back then, even the stuff I grabbed at 320kbps, they just sound like crap. The bass is terrible, the midrange…well don't get me started. Some of those albums have degraded down to 32 or even 16kbps. FLAC rips from the same period still sound great, even if they weren't stored correctly, in a cool, dry place. Seriously, stick to FLAC, you may not be able to hear the difference now, but in a year or two, you'll be glad you did.

item.title: Humans Struggle to Accurately Identify AI Music, Study Reveals
item.description:
Diffusion models for creating music don’t compose songs the same way a human might, by starting with chords and adding vocals and drums. Instead, these models generate the noise of music all at once—visualized by a waveform. With hundreds of millions of waveforms from human generated songs, AI platforms like Suno and Udio can create a model capable of generating AI music.
“A model is fed millions of clips of existing songs, each labeled with a description. To generate a new song, it starts with pure random noise and works backward to create a new waveform. The path it takes to do so is shaped by the words someone puts into the prompt,” O’Donnell writes of these AI services. That backwards generation is the exact opposite of how humans write music—but the human ear struggles to differentiate from the two.
While major labels are suing both Suno and Udio for training their models on copyrighted music at an “unimaginable scale,” these companies argue that training models are fair use. Udio says it has model filters in place to prevent the model from “reproducing copyrighted works or artists’ voices.”
O’Donnell spent a few days playing around with Udio’s model for a test. Generating 30-second samples, he created tracks in 12 genres of music and asked the newsroom team at MIT Technology Review to identify the songs made by AI amid other songs created by people.
“The average score was 46%,” O’Donnell reveals. “And for a few genres, especially instrumental ones, listeners were wrong more often than not.” O’Donnell says when he watched people take the test, he noticed that qualities they confidently flagged as AI compositions—fake-sounding instruments, weird lyrics—were not always right.
“Predictably, people did worse in genres they were less familiar with; some did okay on country or soul, but many stood no chance against jazz, classical piano, or pop. Beaty, the creativity researcher scored 66%, while Brandt, the composer, scored 50%.” With just a few text prompts, O’Donnell created music that humans couldn’t pick out of a line-up as AI generated. “A few could have been easily played at a party without raising objections, and I found two I genuinely loved, even as a lifelong musicians and generally picky music person,” he shares.

item.title: Irish Rap Group Kneecap ‘Blindsides’ Coachella Organizers with Israeli Protests During Weekend 2
item.description:
Coachella organizers Goldenvoice and AEG are facing backlash from Jewish groups for the Irish rap group Kneecap’s performance during both weekends. The performances came with anti-Israeli messaging and criticized the U.S. support of Israel.
Kneecap’s first weekend performance was cut from the Coachella livestream. Coachella organizers appeared to respond by not broadcasting any acts from the Sonora tent during the second weekend on the livestream. Kneecap claimed they were being censored and promised to return with an ‘uncensored’ message—sharing images of their set on social media.
The set contained several messages displayed in bold lettering on stage including ‘Israel is committing genocide against the Palestinian people’ and ‘It is being enabled by the US government who arm and fund Israel despite their war crimes,’ followed by a bold ‘Fuck Israel, Free Palestine’ statement.
Kneecap’s explicit anti-Israel stance during their set at Coachella has led to significant backlash from Jewish organizations. The Creative Community for Peace (CCFP) was among the first to warn Coachella organizers about Kneecap’s record of supporting groups like Hezbollah, which the United States has designated a terrorist group. The CCFP says platforming artists who “promote or sympathize with terrorism undermines the core values of art, music, and unity that Coachella claims to stand for.”
CCFP has demanded a public apology from Goldenvoice and AEG for platforming the group. “Festivals such as Coachella are meant to bring people together to celebrate music and life, instead they allowed the festival to devolve into a forum of hate—platforming a band that praised a terrorist group that carried out the largest massacre in music history,” CCFP Executive Director Ari Ingel stated. “At a time of record levels of antisemitism, it is outrageous that AEG and Goldenvoice allowed this to happen.”
The Tribe of Nova Foundation also condemned Kneecap’s statements and lamented Coachella becoming a platform for the glorification of terror. The group represents survivors and families of the Nova Music Festival massacre attacked by terrorists on October 7, 2023.
“We invite the members of Kneecap to visit the Nova Exhibition and experience firsthand the stories of those who were murdered, those who survived, and those who are still being held hostage. Not to shame or silence—but to connect. To witness. To understand. Healing begins with listening. And we believe that even those who have spoken from a place of anger or misinformation are capable of empathy—if they are willing to see.”
Scooter Braun also spoke out about the incident on Instagram, directly addressing Coachella founder Paul Tollett.
“When I invited Paul to the opening of the Nova music exhibit in Los Angeles, he was the first person from the industry to accept,” Braun said. Braun continues stating he appreciates Tollett’s engagement with the Jewish community, but said the decision to host Kneecap both weekends was ‘blindsiding’ and ‘insensitive.’
